global_fields.name: num_edges

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or number) of one shelf in an adjacency pair. When listed with 'v' it denotes that this shelf is adjacent to the other shelf, so a panel on either shelf would cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or number) of the other shelf in the adjacency pair. Together with 'u' it specifies two neighboring shelves; adjacency is undirected so the order does not affect coverage.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint server of a direct network link. This ID names a server that is adjacent to the server named by the corresponding 'v' field; placing an agent on either endpoint covers the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint server of the direct network link. Together with 'server_a_id' this defines an undirected connection between two servers in the network map.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct forest clearings on the map (i.e., the number of vertices). Each clearing is a potential site for a camera trap; this tells you how many vertices must be covered.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected sightlines between clearings (i.e., the number of edges). Each sightline means the two connected clearings can see each other so a camera in one would cover the other.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exhibit rooms in the museum layout (each graph vertex). Every one of these rooms must be either occupied by a guard or be adjacent to a room that is occupied.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct doorways connecting pairs of rooms (each undirected graph edge counted once). A doorway means a guard in either connected room can observe the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one room at one end of a doorway. Paired with 'room_b' to describe an undirected doorway between two exhibit rooms.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other room at the other end of the doorway. If either room in this pair is staffed by a guard, the other is considered observed.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of gates in the cluster (number of vertices). This tells you how many gates need coverage when choosing where to place crew posts.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected adjacency relationships between gates (number of edges). Use this to verify the adjacency list length and to understand how many neighbor connections exist.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one end of an adjacency pair: the first gate in an undirected adjacent pair. Paired with 'v' to indicate that these two gates are next to each other (so a crew post at one covers the other).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other end of an adjacency pair: the second gate in an undirected adjacent pair. Together with 'u', it defines which two gates are neighbors for coverage purposes.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of attractions (rides) in the park that must be covered. Use this to know how many distinct ride identifiers exist and to check that every ride is included in the staffing coverage.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between attractions. Each adjacency is an undirected connection meaning if one ride in the pair is staffed, the other is considered covered.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one attraction in an adjacency pair. This denotes one endpoint of an undirected adjacency: staffing this ride covers itself and any rides adjacent to it (including the paired ride).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other attraction in the adjacency pair. Together with 'ride_a_id' it defines an undirected adjacency between two rides, meaning staffing either ride covers the other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of substations in the grid layout — the number of vertices the operator must cover (each substation is a node to be powered or adjacent to a powered one).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct connections (bidirectional links) between substations in the layout — the number of edges representing adjacency relationships the operator can use to cover neighbouring substations.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one end of a direct link between substations (a substation ID). Each edge item lists two endpoints; this is the first endpoint of that connection.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other end of a direct link between substations (a substation ID). Together with the 'u' field it defines an undirected adjacency the operator can use to power nearby substations.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of social groups/clubs that need coverage — each is a vertex in the graph and represents a group that either must host someone or be adjacent to a group that does.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of undirected connections between groups — each edge represents a direct link through which a host in one group can cover the other (i.e., adjacency that allows shared coverage).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a connection: the identifier for the first social group in a pair that are directly connected (a host in either group can cover the other).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a connection: the identifier for the second social group in a directly connected pair.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of theater rooms in the cinema complex (i.e., the number of vertices in the graph). Use this to know how many rooms must be covered by placing preview screens so each room either contains a screen or shares a wall with one.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of theaters that share a wall (i.e., the number of undirected edges). Each edge indicates two rooms that are adjacent and therefore can cover each other if one contains a preview screen.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of a shared-wall relationship. This is the ID of the first theater in a pair that share a wall; together with the matching 'v' entry it denotes two adjacent rooms where a screen in either room would cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of a shared-wall relationship. This is the ID of the second theater in the pair that share a wall; combined with the matching 'u' entry it denotes adjacency used to determine coverage by a preview screen.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bike-share docks (vertices) in the system — i.e., how many individual docks must be covered by kiosks or by a neighboring dock that has one.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships (undirected edges) between docks — each counts a pair of neighboring docks where a kiosk at either dock would cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one dock in an adjacent pair; this dock is a candidate location for a repair kiosk and covers itself and any neighboring dock listed with it.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other dock in the adjacent pair; together with dock_u this undirected pair means a kiosk at either dock would cover both docks.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct library branches in the cluster — each branch is a vertex that must be covered (either has a librarian posted or is next door to a branch that does).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected adjacency relationships between branches — each edge represents a pair of branches that are next door to each other (mutual adjacency).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of an adjacency pair: the first branch in a next-door relationship. Together with 'v' this indicates the two neighboring branches involved.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of an adjacency pair: the second branch in a next-door relationship. Together with 'u' this indicates the two neighboring branches involved.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of distinct parking bays in the lot plan; equals the number of vertices in the graph and tells you how many bays must be covered either by an attendant or by an adjacent bay with an attendant.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacent bay pairs in the lot plan; equals the number of undirected adjacency connections (edges) indicating which bays are next to each other for coverage purposes.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one parking bay in a specific adjacency pair; used together with 'bay_endpoint_b' to indicate two bays that abut each other (an undirected adjacency).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other parking bay in the adjacency pair; paired with 'bay_endpoint_a' to show that these two bays are adjacent and one can cover the other if an attendant is stationed at either bay.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of corridors in the building layout. Each corridor is a vertex that may get a camera or be covered by an adjacent corridor's camera.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between corridors. Each edge represents a pair of corridors that are directly beside each other (undirected) and is counted once.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one end of an adjacency: the first corridor in a directly-beside pair. Placing a camera in this corridor covers itself and any corridor listed as adjacent to it.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other end of an adjacency: the second corridor in a directly-beside pair. The pair (corridor_u, corridor_v) denotes two corridors that are next to each other; order does not matter.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of houses on the block being considered. Each house is a vertex and corresponds to one mailbox that may be locked; every house must be covered by a locked mailbox either at itself or at a neighboring house.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between houses (undirected edges). Each count is a pair of neighboring houses that share a fence/porch or are otherwise adjacent; locking one mailbox in the pair protects the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one house in an adjacent pair. This house is adjacent to the house identified by 'v' (the order shown does not imply direction, since adjacency is mutual).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other house in an adjacent pair. Together with 'u' this denotes an undirected adjacency: locking the mailbox at either house covers the other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of intersections (vertices) in the city map — i.e., how many junctions must be covered by a streetlight or an adjacent lit junction.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected streets (edges) connecting intersections; each street links two intersections and defines adjacency for coverage.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint intersection for a given street (one junction at the end of the street). Used together with 'intersection_v' to specify which two intersections are adjacent.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint intersection for the same street (the junction at the other end). Together with 'intersection_u' it defines an undirected connection between two intersections.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of employees on the floor (number of distinct people that must be covered by team leads). Use this to verify that every person is either chosen as a lead or works directly with at least one chosen lead.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct working relationships (undirected pairs of employees who work directly together). This helps confirm the list of who can cover whom when a person is made a team lead.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a direct working relationship: the identifier for one employee in a pair who work directly together. If either employee in the pair is chosen as a team lead, the other is considered covered.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of a direct working relationship: the identifier for the second employee in a pair who work directly together. This undirected pair (employee_a, employee_b) indicates mutual coverage if either is selected as a lead.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of villages in the region (each village has a clinic). This tells you how many vertex identifiers to expect on the map; you must ensure every one is covered by staffing a clinic there or in a neighboring village.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bordering pairs of villages (undirected adjacency links). Each count represents a pair of villages where staffing a specialist in either village will cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one village in a bordering pair (as shown on the map). If you staff the clinic at this village, any village it borders (listed with it) will be considered covered.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other village in the bordering pair. The pair (village_id_a, village_id_b) indicates the two villages share a border so staffing either clinic covers both.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of offices (vertices) in the building that must be covered by routers. Each office is identified by a unique label or number.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of hallway connections (undirected edges) between offices. Each hallway links two offices and allows one office's router to cover the adjacent office.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint office of a hallway connection. Given as the identifier (label or number) of the first office connected by this hallway.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint office of the same hallway connection. Given as the identifier (label or number) of the second office connected by this hallway. The hallway is undirected: office_a and office_b are mutually adjacent.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of trailheads on the park map (the number of vertices in the graph). Every one of these must be covered by the ranger assignment policy (either a ranger is posted there or at an adjacent trailhead).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct connections between trailheads (the number of undirected edges). Each connection indicates two trailheads are adjacent so a ranger stationed at one would also cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one endpoint trailhead of a direct connection. Combined with 'v' this defines an adjacent pair; a ranger at either endpoint covers both trailheads.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other endpoint trailhead of a direct connection. Together with 'u' it marks two adjacent trailheads, indicating coverage can be provided from either location.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of storefronts (shops) in the strip mall. This is the count of vertices: every one must be covered either by displaying a poster itself or by being adjacent to a storefront that does.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacency relationships between storefronts. Each edge represents an undirected neighboring pair of shops where a poster in one can cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one storefront in an adjacent pair. Paired with 'storefront_b' to indicate two neighboring shops; either shop holding a poster would cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other storefront in the adjacent pair. Used with 'storefront_a' to specify an undirected adjacency in the layout.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of classrooms on the school map (each vertex). This is how many rooms must be covered by monitors either directly or via an adjacent room.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency connections between classrooms (each undirected edge). Each count represents two neighboring rooms that share a wall/door so a monitor in one can supervise the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The label/identifier of one classroom in an adjacent pair. Together with 'v' this denotes two neighboring rooms; order is irrelevant because adjacency is undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The label/identifier of the other classroom in the adjacent pair. Paired with 'u' it marks two neighboring rooms where a monitor in either room covers the other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of campsites along the stretch (the number of vertices in the graph). Used to know how many sites must be covered and to compare the number of posts placed against the minimum possible.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The number of undirected adjacency connections between campsites (the number of edges). Each adjacency means the two listed campsites are neighbors so a post at one would cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of an adjacency pair: the identifier (label or index) of the first campsite in a neighboring relationship. In a pair (u,v) this campsite is adjacent to campsite_b.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of an adjacency pair: the identifier of the second campsite in the neighboring relationship. Together with campsite_a, it denotes two campsites that are adjacent so a post at either covers the other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total count of bike-rack locations on the map (the number of vertices). Each rack is a candidate to be designated as a maintenance hub or to be covered by a neighboring hub.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of undirected adjacency connections between racks (the number of edges). Each adjacency means the two connected racks sit next to each other so a hub at one would cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the first bike rack endpoint of an adjacency. Used to reference a specific rack location on the map.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the second bike rack endpoint of an adjacency. Together with 'rack_u_id', it denotes two racks that are next to each other.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of households (houses/residences) on the block; this is the number of vertices that must be covered by ambassadors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency relationships between households; each counts a pair of neighboring houses (an edge) where an ambassador at one house would cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the first household in a neighboring pair — one endpoint of an adjacency indicating this house is next door to the other listed house.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the second household in a neighboring pair — the other endpoint of an adjacency indicating this house is next door to the first listed house.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of blocks in the council area (each block corresponds to a vertex where at most one notice board can be installed). Use this to know how many blocks must be covered.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of blocks that share a boundary (each edge indicates two blocks that are adjacent so a board in one covers the other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one block in an adjacent pair; this block shares a boundary with the block given by 'v', meaning a board in either one would cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other block in an adjacent pair; together with 'u' it denotes two blocks that touch and thus can cover each other if one has a notice board.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of food stalls in the festival food court. Stall identifiers run from 1 up to this number; this tells the solver how many positions must be covered by chefs or their neighbors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of direct adjacency relationships (side-by-side connections) between stalls. Each counted adjacency represents a pair of stalls where a chef at one would cover the other; the count treats each undirected adjacency once.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one stall in an adjacency pair. Together with 'v' this specifies two stalls that are directly adjacent (side-by-side), meaning a chef placed at either stall would cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other stall in an adjacency pair. Paired with 'u', it denotes an undirected adjacency between two stalls (side-by-side).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of plazas in the event area — the number of vertices in the graph. This tells you how many distinct plazas need coverage (either by hosting an active hotspot or by being adjacent to one).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency pairs (undirected edges) between plazas. Each pair represents two plazas that are neighbors, meaning a hotspot at one would also cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One plaza identifier of an adjacency pair. Paired with 'v', it denotes that plaza_a and plaza_b are neighboring plazas (an undirected edge), so activating a hotspot at either will cover the other.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other plaza identifier of an adjacency pair. Together with 'u' this defines a neighbor relationship between plaza_b and plaza_a; order does not matter because adjacency is undirected.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of river sections in this network (i.e., the number of vertices). Use this to know how many sections must be covered by sensors or adjacent to a sensor.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency connections between river sections (i.e., the number of undirected edges). Each connection indicates two sections that touch so a sensor on one would cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint of a connection: the label for the first river section in this adjacent pair. This denotes a section that is directly connected to the section given by 'v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint of a connection: the label for the second river section in this adjacent pair. Together with 'u', it defines two sections that touch and therefore can cover each other if one has a sensor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of communities (neighborhoods) in the town — equivalent to the number of vertices. This is how many distinct places must be covered by libraries (either directly or via an adjacent neighborhood).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacency links between neighborhoods — equivalent to the number of undirected edges. Each counts a pair of neighborhoods that are considered adjacent (so a library in one would cover the other).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint of an adjacency: the ID of a neighborhood that is adjacent to the neighborhood given by 'v'. Opening a library here would cover this neighborhood and any neighborhoods listed as adjacent to it.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint of an adjacency: the ID of a neighborhood adjacent to the neighborhood given by 'u'. The pair (u, v) denotes an undirected adjacency between two neighborhoods.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of gates in the facility (the number of vertices in the graph). This tells you how many distinct gate locations must be covered either by posting a guard at the gate or by having a guard at an adjacent gate.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct adjacencies between gates (the number of undirected edges). Each connection means a guard posted at one of those two gates would also cover the other.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a connection: the identifier for one gate in an undirected adjacency pair. A guard at this gate would cover the paired gate listed as 'gate_v'.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the connection: the identifier for the gate adjacent to 'gate_u'. Because adjacencies are undirected, staffing either 'gate_u' or 'gate_v' would cover both.
